text:
Laura (Product): quick sync — proposing a multi-region QoS-floor pilot for Dedicated. Goal: guarantee a latency floor for each tenant (p95 target) during mixed-priority load while still allowing regional spillover. Need scope, success metrics, and launch gates.

Michael (Eng-Infra): curious about where the enforcement lives. Is this routing-level (edge -> region) or runtime-level scheduling?

Laura (Product): thinking routing + admission. routing tags by tenant priority and region, then admission enforces per-tenant reservoir. If region saturated, spillover to secondary region with preempt policy.

Priya (SRE): we need concrete signals. propose: p95 latency by tenant, error-rate by tenant, preempt count, and eviction rate. also a degradation matrix for partial region failures.

Samir (Eng-ML): for model serving we must decide cache partitioning. if KV cache is global the p95 improvements evaporate. I'd prefer per-tenant KV partitions for the pilot.

Eva (Customer Success): FYI — a fintech pilot customer asked for regional isolation + low tail latency for high-priority traffic (regulatory reasons). they'd accept spillover but only after a 5s grace and with audit logs.

Michael (Eng-Infra): what about cost? cross-region spillover increases egress and double-run risk. needs a cost cap and fallback to degraded model (smaller quantized variant).

Laura (Product): agree — include model-variant fallback as one of the mitigation strategies. rough policy sketch: 

```yaml
qos_floor_policy:
  p95_ms: 120
  min_share: 10%
  spill_policy: regional_preempt
  fallback: model_variant: quantized-v2
```

Samir (Eng-ML): prototype note: quantized-v2 has ~1.5x CPU but 0.6x latency in local tests. need to confirm on burst workloads and with KV split.

Priya (SRE): can we simulate a failover + spike? last sim (sim-2024-07-21) with naive spill routing showed a 12% tail spike and double-charged tokens for some requests. we should run a controlled sim: 
- mixed-priority noise (80/20 low/high)
- regional outage (30m)
- 50% cache miss increase

Michael (Eng-Infra): I'll add a routing experiment in staging. need a gate: no >2x billing delta in pilot vs baseline AND p95 under target for high-priority tenants.

Eva (Customer Success): customer requirement: audit trail of every spill over within 1 hour resolution + email alert for >3 spills/hour.

Laura (Product): proposed launch criteria (draft): 
- stability: p95 <= 120ms for high-priority tenants for 72h under synthetic mixed load
- safety: no more than 5% request duplication or double billing artifacts in pilot
- cost: median customer cost delta <= 1.3x baseline for pilot cluster
- observability: runbook + 5s audit log delivery to CS bucket

OpsBot: deployed routing-experiment-v1 -> staging (build 2024-08-02T09:12).

Samir (Eng-ML): action items: I'll spike per-tenant KV partition + quantized-v2 fallback in a sandbox. ETA 2w.

Priya (SRE): I'll draft the incident runbook and the degradation matrix; want to own canary thresholds. ETA 1w.

Michael (Eng-Infra): I'll implement the spillover router and cost-safety limiter in staging; need API shape from Product. ETA 2w.

Laura (Product): I'll assemble launch checklist + customer compliance checklist; will sync with Eva on audit/log delivery. ETA 4 days for checklist.

Eva (Customer Success): I'll coordinate pilot customer expectations and get sign-off on the 5s grace + audit format.

Laura (Product): next sync Friday 10am PT. main deliverables: sim results, runbook draft, routing PR, and cost delta estimate.

Michael (Eng-Infra): noted. adding item: metric to detect "silent spill" where requests spill but user doesn't see increased latency (makes billing mismatch subtle).

Priya (SRE): + test to assert no request duplication under spill (we saw duplication in earlier sim).

Samir (Eng-ML): question for product: should fallback to quantized variant be automatic or operator-triggered during pilot? automatic is better for SLOs but harder for telemetry.

Laura (Product): pilot: operator-triggered but with a well-defined automated fallback if operator misses a threshold for >10m. we can tighten later.

Eva (Customer Success): sounds reasonable to customers. I'll surface the operator-triggered flow in the pilot agreement.

Michael (Eng-Infra): tagging @samir @priya for infra constraints: cross-region cache sync may block per-tenant partitions. we might shard by tenant-id mod N.

Samir (Eng-ML): ok, will prototype tenant-shard mapping. note: might require minor model loader changes.

Laura (Product): great. I'll update the roadmap doc and link the pilot ticket once Michael creates the routing PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
